text:
Maya Patel: Quick sync: several partners reported 400s when they accidentally sent X-API-Version: 2026-01. Looks like gateway is strict. We need a safe opt-in compatibility probe rather than immediate permissive fallback.
Ethan Cole: Saw that. Current behavior rejects unknown versions during header validation. Proposal: add 'probe mode' that lets unknown versions through to a compat handler and attaches a response header 'X-Compat-Mode: probe'.
Ravi Kapoor: For SDKs we should expose an opt-in switch so customers using old SDKs can enable probe without server-side feature flags. SDKs should not throw on unknown version; instead surface a warning and allow retry.
Sofia Nguyen: Operational concerns: must ensure probe path doesn't incur heavy schema conversion CPU. Add a sampling cap per-tenant and backpressure if conversions exceed threshold.
Maya Patel: Concrete behavior idea:
- If X-Compat-Opt: probe or tenant flagged, do lightweight accept and forward to compat-router.
- If compat-router detects missing required fields for new shape, return 422 with body explaining the required field and include X-Compat-Error: missing_field.
- Otherwise, process using latest-compatible model and add X-Compat-Mode: probe in response.
Ethan Cole: Middleware sketch (pseudo):
```js
// gateway middleware
const version = req.get('X-API-Version')
if (!KNOWN_VERSIONS.has(version)) {
  if (req.get('X-Compat-Opt') === 'probe' || tenantConfig.probeEnabled) {
    req.set('X-Compat-Probe', '1')
    // attach original client version for telemetry
    req.ctx.meta.client_version = version || 'unspecified'
    next() // route to compat-router
  } else {
    return res.status(400).send({error: 'unknown api version'})
  }
}
```
Ravi Kapoor: SDK changes: js/python SDKs to add compatOpt: 'probe' option, log a one-time warning to console, and include header. We'll add unit tests to ensure we don't silently swallow errors.
Sofia Nguyen: Metrics / dashboards: capture compat_probe_rate{tenant,client_version}, compat_fallback_success, compat_fallback_error_type, and latency delta between normal and compat routes. Add alert: if compat_fallback_error_rate > 2% for any tenant with >1000 reqs/hour, page oncall.
Maya Patel: Rollout plan: feature-flag the gateway change. Canary 0.2% for 12h, if no spike -> 2% for 24h -> 10% for 48h. Enable tenant opt-in immediately via tenant flag UI for partners that want testing.
Ethan Cole: Implementation notes: keep compat-router fast, avoid costly DB lookups; prefer schema-driven validation in memory. Add a circuit-breaker that short-circuits to 400 if conversion queue grows.
ci-bot: ci: unit tests for gateway middleware + 3 integration fixtures queued (build/job/5241)
Ravi Kapoor: Also recommend we add a non-blocking response header 'Warning: 299 CompatProbe' with short text that SDKs can surface to end users. That gives visibility without forcing clients to parse custom headers.
Sofia Nguyen: Test plan: synthetics that send variants of unknown versions, run at 5qps per tenant over 1h, and compare p50/p95 and error counts. Add chaos test to simulate a compat-router slowdown and assert circuit-breaker trips gracefully.
Maya Patel: Action items: Ethan -> gateway middleware + FF (PR by Thu). Ravi -> SDK opt-in + warning (PR by Thu). Sofia -> dashboards and alerts + synthetic suites (by Mon). I'll draft a one-paragraph partner note and an eng-platform runbook entry for when to flip FF off if we see consumer regressions.
Ethan Cole: I'll include a small test harness and a fallback header X-Compat-Fallback: latest when we actually used a fallback path.
Ravi Kapoor: A small compatibility nuance: some clients embed version in body; we'll not attempt body transforms in probe mode, only header-driven routing. If body shape is incompatible, compat-router returns 422.
Maya Patel: Good call. Keep probe conservative. We'll iterate after the canary and revert quickly if breakers trip. Thanks all.
